candidate.title: TAB-Seq
candidate.scope: The TAB-Seq (Tet-assisted bisulfite sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina poster: genomic DNA bearing 5hmC undergoes βGT glucosylation, TET oxidation, and the combined depicted bisulfite-treatment/PCR-amplification block to produce DNA encoding original 5hmC positions as retained C. The left 5hmc residue icon identifies the biological target; the five-base cartoons illustrate modification classes, not an asserted genomic sequence. The card title and matching page-92 heading/caption establish this single target. MAB-seq, RRMAB-seq and MIRA are adjacent independent rows, not alternatives or branches of TAB-Seq. The partial chemical legend at the right is context. No branch, pooling, capture, adapter structure or sequencing operation is drawn within this row; the extraction ends at its amplified DNA output and explains the supported sequencing interpretation.

features: The schematic base-call pattern is T T C T T for the input classes C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC, respectively; the final unlabeled blue segment is captioned DNA.

evidence.quote: Successful detection of 5hmC is governed by three key parameters: 1) efficient conversion of unmodified cytosine to uracil; 2) efficient conversion of 5mC to 5caU/U; and 3) efficient protection of 5hmC.

operations.label: βGT / Glucosylation
operations.description: βGT transfers glucose onto 5hmC in the input DNA, changing that modification into 5gmC. The other depicted cytosine classes remain unchanged at this step.
operations.mechanism: β-Glucosyltransferase-mediated glucosylation protects the original 5hmC from the subsequent TET oxidation. βGT is the catalyst for this single DNA route.
operations.information_effect: Protection marks the original 5hmC positions chemically within their native DNA sequence context, establishing the selective survival that will later yield C base calls.

operations.label: TET / Oxidation
operations.description: The glucosylated DNA is oxidized: the diagram changes original 5mC and 5fC positions into 5caC, retains pre-existing 5caC, and leaves protected 5gmC and unmodified C as drawn.
operations.mechanism: The diagram labels the catalyst TET; the matched primary implementation uses recombinant mouse Tet1 catalytic domain. The glucose on 5gmC blocks further TET oxidation of the target, whereas original 5mC is oxidized to the bisulfite-sensitive 5caC endpoint. The depicted original-5fC-to-5caC change is directly supported by the drawing.
operations.information_effect: This makes original 5mC converge with other bisulfite-sensitive positions while preserving original 5hmC as a distinct protected class. The identities of the individual non-target modification classes will be lost in the final T readout.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: The oxidized, glucosylated DNA undergoes the combined depicted bisulfite treatment and PCR amplification block. Bisulfite changes unmodified C and 5caC to uracil or 5caU, respectively, while original 5hmC remains protected as 5gmC. After amplification, the depicted positions read T T C T T, and the product is labeled DNA.
operations.mechanism: Differential bisulfite susceptibility followed by PCR converts chemical modification differences into an ordinary DNA sequence code: protected 5gmC is read as C, whereas C and the 5caC positions read as T. The single composite block is retained at the figure's resolution.
operations.information_effect: At corresponding genomic cytosine positions, retained C supports base-resolution identification of original 5hmC, subject to conversion and protection efficiencies. In the paper's CG interpretation, the C fraction among C/T calls estimates hydroxymethylation abundance. Traditional bisulfite sequencing can provide the complementary total-modification measurement used to estimate 5mC; that comparison is paper-supported interpretation, not a second branch or operation drawn in this schematic.
